ETH100
                            Glossary

      Citizenship
The status of being a member of a particular country or community and the rights,
duties, and responsibilities associated with it.
      Civic Rights
Rights guaranteed to individuals by law to participate in civic and political life, such
as the right to vote and freedom of expression.
      Civic Responsibilities
Duties and obligations that citizens are expected to fulfill in order to contribute to
the common good and maintain a functioning society.
      Political Engagement
Active participation in political processes and institutions, including voting,
advocacy, and grassroots activism.
      Social Justice
The fair and equitable distribution of resources, opportunities, and rights within
society, with a focus on addressing systemic inequalities and promoting human
dignity.
      Community Engagement
Collaborative efforts by individuals and groups to address shared challenges and
improve the well-being of their communities through volunteerism, advocacy, and
collective action.
Maha Malik’s Compilation

      Global Citizenship
A sense of belonging to a broader community beyond national borders, with a
commitment to promoting human rights, sustainability, and solidarity on a global
scale.
      Ethical Leadership
Leadership characterized by integrity, accountability, and a commitment to ethical
principles, with a focus on serving the common good and fostering positive social
change.
      Civic Empowerment
The process of enabling individuals and communities to participate actively in
decision-making processes, advocate for their interests, and effect change in their
environments.
      Reflective Practice
A deliberate process of self-awareness and critical reflection on one's values, beliefs,
and actions, with the goal of continuous learning and personal growth.

Topic 001: Why this course?
We are taking this course because we want to learn the reasons why we are not doing well as a society. It
will help us in realization, worry, planning, and sharing ideas with others on how to become a better citizen.

Topic 002: What makes effective citizenship?
First, we will learn what makes an effective citizenship. The first thing is a sense of responsibility which is
an internal feeling about fulfilling the responsibility. The second point is empathy, which is feeling the
pains of others and assessing how they are facing challenges in their life. The third point is patriotism which
means loving your country and trying to make it better in every matter.

Topic 003: Why effective citizenship?
We will learn about the incentives and benefits of being an incentive citizen. Firstly, I will do better if I
become an effective citizen. Secondly, it has benefits in this life as well as in the hereafter.

Topic 004: Effective citizenship: Duties of citizen
Every citizen has some duties to perform. The first duty is loyalty to the state and obedience to the
Constitution. A citizen must follow the constitution in every aspect of life and be loyal to the state in all
matters. Article 5 makes it binding on every citizen to be loyal to the state. The state has institutions that
are legally bound to follow the constitution. Territories, objectives, and laws all can be changed within the
limits of the Constitution."

Topic 005: Rights of citizen: Freedom of life and liberty
A citizen must be aware of the rights of other citizens. Article 9 ensures the right to life and liberty. It means
one citizen cannot take the life of another citizen or injure him for whatever reason. One citizen cannot
attack or harm another and cannot interfere in his personal life. Liberty and freedom cannot be taken away
from any citizen.

Topic 006: Rights of citizen: Fair trial
Every person is entitled to a fair trial in which judges will make their decision about it. No institution will
interfere in the process of a fair trial. If a person cannot afford a fair trial, then the Constitution ensures that
he will be compensated so that he can have a fair trial. There cannot be a media trial before the final
judgment.

Topic 007: Rights of citizen: Slavery
A citizen cannot be made a slave under any circumstances. Article 11 forbids all kinds of slavery and forced
labor. A citizen cannot be forced to do labor for which he has not applied. It is against the constitution of
Pakistan.

Topic 008: Rights of citizen: Freedom of movement
According to Article 15, all citizens have the right to move freely and settle in any area of Pakistan unless
it is a prohibited area. All areas of all the cities are open for its citizens. Except the private houses and
institutions where permission is required to enter. The idea is to bring the Pakistanis together.

Topic 009: Rights of citizen: Right of access to information
Article 19 ensures that every citizen has the right to access the information unless that information is
prohibited. A citizen can apply from the relevant institution for the required information. However, any
public interest or information that can be misused can be prohibited from public access.

Topic 010: Rights of citizen: Religious Freedom
Articles 20,21,22 ensures the right to choose a religion, preach it, and establish a religious institution.
Nobody is bound to follow any religion other than his own. Admission should not be denied in educational
institutions based on religious background. All citizens must have equal opportunities for freedom and
participation.

Topic 011: Rights of citizen: Freedom to own and sell property
Articles 23 and 24 ensure that every citizen can buy or sell property anywhere at any time in the country.
For the interest of special communities or areas, there can be some restrictions on the sale and purchase of
the land or property because of its conflicting status. The constitution of Pakistan guarantees this right to
its citizens so that the citizens can feel belongingness with their land and country and their relationship can
become stronger.

Topic 012: Rights of citizen: Protection to language and culture
Article 28 ensures that every group having a distinct language or culture holds the right to promote their
language and culture. The idea is to enrich diversity. It increases the positive qualities among the people
and encourages critical thinking. This opportunity is to bring a feeling of belonging to the country and build
a stronger connection with its country.

                               Short Questions
1. Enlist any three types of commitments.

      Reaching a place on time.
      Starting a program on time.
      Finishing a program on time.

2. Why should we create associations and clubs for coordination of good initiatives in
society?

      To bring together people with similar interests.
      To share ideas, experiences, and skills.
      To help people learn from one another.
      To promote cooperation and build a better society.

3. Why should we treat the elderly with respect?

      They have valuable life experience and wisdom.
      Respect strengthens family and social relationships.
      It reflects good character and promotes a caring society.

4. Role of an effective citizen in community development.

      Helps others financially, physically, and through advice.
      Participates in community service.
      Coordinates good initiatives.
      Protects the environment.
      Follows laws and encourages positive values.

5. Why should we treat transgender people with respect?

      Every human deserves dignity and equal respect.
      Discrimination weakens society.
      Respect promotes equality, harmony, and inclusion.

6. Importance of effective time management.

      Increases productivity.
      Reduces stress.
      Helps achieve goals.
      Prevents procrastination.
      Creates a balance between work and personal life.

7. Mention three ways of helping others.

      Financial help.
      Giving your time.
      Giving advice and guidance.

8. "Evil is spread like a disease." Briefly explain.
If evil is not discouraged, it spreads throughout society. Silence encourages wrongdoing,
influences others to commit similar acts, weakens moral values, and creates injustice. Therefore,
evil should be discouraged wisely, at the right time, and in the right manner.

9. Correction topic (Self-correction).
Self-correction means identifying your own mistakes and improving them. A person who
corrects himself develops confidence, improves his personality, and becomes a better citizen.

                                Long Questions
1. If you have to read a paper for a school assignment, write five facilities to help you in
comprehension.

      Read with full concentration.
      Understand the meaning of unfamiliar words using a dictionary.
      Pay attention to punctuation marks.
      Read at your own suitable pace.
      Avoid casual reading and read critically.

2. If an employer creates a congenial working environment, how will it benefit employees?
(Write any two benefits.)

      Employees become more motivated and productive.
      Better cooperation, teamwork, and positive relationships develop among employees.

3. "Encouragement is necessary for promoting virtue in a society." Discuss.

Encouragement motivates people to continue doing good deeds. Appreciating virtuous actions
strengthens positive behavior and inspires others to follow. Good people may become
discouraged without support, so encouragement helps maintain motivation, moral values, and a
culture of kindness. It should always be sincere and free from exaggeration.

4. How can we encourage virtue in society?

      Appreciate and praise good deeds.
      Encourage kindness and helping others.
      Promote honesty and truthfulness.
      Motivate people through good examples.
